summary: Ives Waldo works in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer (1929–2011) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a lecturer at Charles University around 1960 and was affiliated with the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology around 1970.

Iwao Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held appointments as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Iwao Nakajima (born 1934) studied under Nichiki Kimura and completed a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, he worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and served as head at Sandhaan around 1999.

Iwao Shima (1950–2007) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya University from roughly 1969 to 1978 and later served on the faculty at Kanazawa University from circa 1989, becoming a professor in 1996.

Izumi Hoshi (born 1967) is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo between 1987 and 1997. She joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as assistant professor in 1997 and served as director from 2019 to 2023.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami specializes in Japanology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and is attested as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington.

J. A. B. van Buitenen (1928–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, taught at Utrecht, and served as the George V. Bobrinskoy Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago.

J. B. Disanayaka (born 1937) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from circa 1982 to 2002 and held a post at SOAS University of London around 1996.

J. G. Jennings was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Principal of Muir Central College and as Director of Public Instruction for the Department of Public Instruction, Bihar and Orissa, attested in 1918.

J. Gordon Melton (born 1942) is a religious studies scholar educated at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held professorships at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.

J. L. Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Bimal Krishna Matilal and earned a degree from Rice University (1969–1973). He was on the faculty at Victoria University of Wellington from circa 1974 to 2014.
J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from roughly 1891 to 1923.
J. N. Farquhar (1861–1929) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He was educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1883–1885), and Christ Church (~1885–1889).

J. P. Mallory (born 1945) is a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Occidental College and UCLA, he served as Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University Belfast from circa 1997 to 2011.

J. Robert Oppenheimer (1904–1967) studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and studied under Arthur W. Ryder. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, the Manhattan Project, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

J. S. Negi is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi, conducted research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University around 1977, and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
J. S. Pade was an Indologist who served as a Research Officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

J. Thomas Rimer (born 1933) is a Japanologist educated at Princeton and Columbia. He held faculty posts at Washington University in St. Louis, UCLA, the University of Maryland, College Park, and the University of Pittsburgh.
